doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: The piano in the house and his father's button accordion
summary: His brother moved a piano into the house, showed him middle C, and his father played Slovak button accordion polkas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I assume you had a piano in the house?

Yeah. My brother was finishing his college degree when I was about 5 or 6 years old, or he was in college and he moved a piano into our house, and there was a piano because he needed it for whatever you need to do to pass piano in college. So there it was. And Joe showed me middle C and some notes, and kind of from there got to some lessons, and then trying to pick out tunes.
Did your father, he played a button accordion?
Yeah, what do they call those, harmonium, or — it’s a button accordion, you know the bass has buttons. It’s very, very Slavic sort of, eastern European.
